name: DeskVNC
description: DeskVNC is a native desktop client for VNC, RDP and SSH, written in Rust on Tauri 2 and running on Windows, macOS and Linux. It ships an MCP server named dvv that lets an AI agent drive the same remote desktop connections a person uses, with nothing installed on the remote machine and a person able to take the wheel back at any moment.
softwareRequirements: Tauri 2 system dependencies for the host platform. Building from source requires Rust 1.95 or newer and Node 22 or newer.
featureList: VNC client (RFB 3.3 to 3.8) with VeNCrypt, RA2 and Apple authentication
RDP client with NLA, RemoteApp, resolution control, and the usual codecs
SSH client with terminal, SFTP file transfer, tunnels, and PuTTY key files
MCP server named dvv for AI agent control of remote desktops
AI agent loop with dvv_hosts, dvv_open, dvv_control, dvv_screen, dvv_click, dvv_type, dvv_key
Multi-machine parallel control: every machine is its own limb with its own lease
Coordinate fencing with screen generation to refuse clicks computed against a stale screen
Typing fencing that refuses dvv_type and dvv_key if the screen has repainted
Human takeover at any moment without stranding a held key or a half finished drag
Saved host library with one double click to connect
Operating system keychain credential storage (Keychain Services, Credential Manager, Secret Service)
Encrypted file fallback credential storage for headless machines
Live thumbnails of every saved machine
Tabbed sessions with split panes, each pane on a different machine and protocol
Bidirectional clipboard integration
Bidirectional SFTP file transfer
Reconnection after drops with a clear report of what happened
Screenshots, fullscreen mode, and view only mode
Display and input controls with scroll wheel and trackpad direction preserved
Keyboard layouts, dead keys, and CJK input methods preserved end to end
Network discovery via mDNS browsing, subnet scanning with banner fingerprinting, mDNS, LLMNR, NetBIOS, and MS-RPC name resolution
Wake on LAN
WebGL2 frame painting for low overhead decoding in Rust
H.264 hardware acceleration where the webview offers it
Boundary based attended support with direct encrypted paths and a relay fallback
Verified integration with Claude Code over stdio and HTTP
Verified integration with OpenCode over stdio and HTTP
Documented integration for Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, VS Code, and plain Python agents
